_note: Spectrum facts as data: `python -m nexclash.kb hw WORD` (address in hex without prefix, or a name). Source: Sinclair ROM disassembly, 48K/128K manuals, the Next wiki; status 'doc' = from documentation, 'hw' = relied on by a build that runs on hardware. Add rows as games need them; Next registers the builds use: docs/NEXT_REGISTERS.md.

memory.name: display file
memory.what: 6144 bytes, 192 lines x 32; address of (y, x/8) = 0x4000 | (y & 0xC0) << 5 | (y & 7) << 8 | (y & 0x38) << 2 | x >> 3; next pixel line: INC H, and at a cell boundary add 0x20 to L, at a third boundary no fix-up of H

memory.name: attribute file
memory.what: 768 bytes, 24 x 32; bit 7 FLASH, 6 BRIGHT, 5-3 PAPER, 2-0 INK; attr address from a display address: H = (H >> 3 & 3) | 0x58

memory.name: printer buffer
memory.what: free on 48K unless the game uses it (scan proves it); 128K BASIC keeps paging variables here

memory.name: system variables
memory.what: see sysvars; a game that never returns to BASIC may reuse them, IM 1 still writes FRAMES and reads keys into LAST_K via 0x0038

memory.name: PROG default
memory.what: start of BASIC program (23755) on an unexpanded 48K

memory.name: 128K paged slot
memory.what: bank 0-7 by port 7FFD bits 0-2; bank 5 is also 0x4000, bank 2 also 0x8000; bank 7 = shadow screen

sysvars.name: KSTATE
sysvars.what: 8 bytes, keyboard state used by the ROM key scan

sysvars.name: LAST_K
sysvars.what: last key pressed (written by the IM 1 handler)

sysvars.name: CHARS
sysvars.what: font address - 256 (default 0x3C00: font at 0x3D00); games point it at their own font

sysvars.name: ERR_NR
sysvars.what: error code - 1; IY points here (IY = 0x5C3A) while the ROM runs

sysvars.name: FLAGS
sysvars.what: BASIC flags; bit 5 = new key available

sysvars.name: ERR_SP
sysvars.what: address of the error return on the stack

sysvars.name: CH_ADD
sysvars.what: address of the next character to interpret

sysvars.name: DF_SZ
sysvars.what: lines in the lower screen (2); 0 lets PRINT use all 24 lines

sysvars.name: FRAMES
sysvars.what: 3-byte frame counter, incremented by the IM 1 handler; games read it for timing and random numbers

sysvars.name: UDG
sysvars.what: address of the first user-defined graphic

sysvars.name: COORDS
sysvars.what: x, y of the last PLOT

sysvars.name: DF_CC
sysvars.what: display file address of the PRINT position

sysvars.name: S_POSN
sysvars.what: 33 - column, 24 - line of the PRINT position

sysvars.name: ATTR_P
sysvars.what: permanent colours (used by CLS and PRINT)

sysvars.name: RAMTOP
sysvars.what: last byte of the BASIC area; code above it is safe from BASIC

sysvars.name: BANKM
sysvars.what: 128K: copy of the last value written to port 7FFD

sysvars.name: BANK678
sysvars.what: +2A/+3: copy of the last value written to port 1FFD

ports.name: ULA
ports.what: IN: bits 0-4 = keys of the half-rows selected by the low bits of the high address byte (0 = pressed), bit 6 = EAR; OUT: bits 0-2 border, bit 3 MIC, bit 4 beeper. Decoded on bit 0 = 0 only: any even port is the ULA

ports.name: keys SHIFT Z X C V
ports.what: half-row, bit 0 = CAPS SHIFT

ports.name: keys A S D F G
ports.what: half-row

ports.name: keys Q W E R T
ports.what: half-row

ports.name: keys 1 2 3 4 5
ports.what: half-row; Sinclair joystick 2 = 1-5 (left right down up fire)

ports.name: keys 0 9 8 7 6
ports.what: half-row, bit 0 = 0; Sinclair joystick 1 = 6-0; cursor joystick 5 6 7 8 0

ports.name: keys P O I U Y
ports.what: half-row, bit 0 = P

ports.name: keys ENTER L K J H
ports.what: half-row, bit 0 = ENTER

ports.name: keys SPACE SYM M N B
ports.what: half-row, bit 0 = SPACE, bit 1 = SYMBOL SHIFT

ports.name: Kempston joystick
ports.what: IN: bit 0 right, 1 left, 2 down, 3 up, 4 fire (1 = active); with no interface the read returns the floating bus, so a game in joystick mode sees phantom input (PLAYBOOK 0)

ports.name: 128K paging
ports.what: OUT: bits 0-2 RAM bank at 0xC000, bit 3 shadow screen, bit 4 ROM (0 = 128 editor, 1 = 48 BASIC), bit 5 lock until reset. Write-only: games keep a copy (BANKM 0x5B5C)

ports.name: +2A/+3 paging
ports.what: OUT: bit 0 special paging, bit 2 ROM high bit, bit 3 disk motor

ports.name: AY register select
ports.what: OUT: register number 0-15; IN: read the selected register

ports.name: AY data
ports.what: OUT: value for the selected register

ports.name: floating bus
ports.what: IN from an unattached port returns the byte the ULA is fetching (attribute or pixel) or 0xFF in the border: games use it to sync to the beam (Arkanoid, Cobra, Sidewize). The Next's floating bus differs by timing mode: check BRIEFING A1 before relying on it

ports.name: Next register select
ports.what: OUT: NextReg number; then port 253B reads / writes it. Hooks use the NEXTREG instruction instead

ports.name: Next register data
ports.what: IN / OUT the selected NextReg

ports.name: Next sprite slot / flags
ports.what: OUT: sprite slot for attribute and pattern upload; IN: bit 0 collision, bit 1 over 12 sprites on a line

ports.name: Next sprite attributes
ports.what: OUT: 4 or 5 attribute bytes per sprite, auto-increment

ports.name: Next sprite pattern
ports.what: OUT: 256 bytes per 8-bit pattern, auto-increment

ports.name: Next Layer 2 access
ports.what: OUT: bit 0 map for write, bit 1 Layer 2 visible, bit 2 map for read, bits 6-7 which third

timing.name: 48K frame
timing.what: 69888 T = 312 lines x 224 T at 3.5 MHz, 50.08 Hz; interrupt at T 0, first display pixel at T 14336 (line 64)

timing.name: 128K frame
timing.what: 70908 T = 311 lines x 228 T at 3.5469 MHz; first display pixel at T 14362

timing.name: interrupt length
timing.what: INT is held 32 T (48K) / 36 T (128K): a handler shorter than that with EI re-enters; IM 2 reads the vector from I x 256 + bus value (usually 0xFF): games fill a 257-byte table with one byte

timing.name: contention
timing.what: the ULA delays the CPU when it touches 0x4000-0x7FFF (128K: also banks 1, 3, 5, 7) or does I/O with a contended address during the display: 6,5,4,3,2,1,0,0 T by position in each 8 T. RZX replay is frame-exact, T counts in survey / cost do not model it

timing.name: R register
timing.what: bits 0-6 count M1 cycles (2 for prefixed opcodes), bit 7 keeps what LD R,A wrote; games read it as a random number: hooks change it unless they preserve R (card patch.preserve-r)

timing.name: HALT
timing.what: waits for the next interrupt = the usual frame sync; a game with interrupts off has none and runs as fast as its code allows

rom48.name: START
rom48.what: reset

rom48.name: ERROR_1
rom48.what: RST 08: BASIC error, code in the byte after the RST

rom48.name: PRINT_A_1
rom48.what: RST 10: print character in A to the current channel (control codes 16-23 set colours / position)

rom48.name: GET_CHAR
rom48.what: RST 18

rom48.name: NEXT_CHAR
rom48.what: RST 20

rom48.name: FP_CALC
rom48.what: RST 28: floating-point calculator, byte codes follow until 0x38

rom48.name: BC_SPACES
rom48.what: RST 30

rom48.name: MASK_INT
rom48.what: IM 1 handler: FRAMES += 1, key scan into LAST_K, EI, RET. Uses AF BC DE HL only, about 1000 T

rom48.name: RESET (NMI)
rom48.what: NMI handler

rom48.name: KEY_SCAN
rom48.what: scan the keyboard: E = key 0-39 or 0xFF, D = shift key; Z set = valid

rom48.name: KEYBOARD
rom48.what: the IM 1 key routine (KEY_SCAN + repeat + LAST_K)

rom48.name: K_TEST
rom48.what: key number to main code

rom48.name: BEEPER
rom48.what: DE = cycles - 1... HL = period: tone on the beeper, interrupts off for its duration

rom48.name: BEEP
rom48.what: BASIC BEEP from the calculator stack

rom48.name: SA_BYTES
rom48.what: save header / data block to tape

rom48.name: LD_BYTES
rom48.what: load a tape block: IX = address, DE = length, A = flag byte, carry = load (not verify)

rom48.name: CLS
rom48.what: clear the whole screen with ATTR_P

rom48.name: CL_ALL
rom48.what: clear the display area

rom48.name: CL_SET
rom48.what: set the print position from BC (line, column as 24 - line, 33 - column)

rom48.name: CL_SC_ALL
rom48.what: scroll the whole display up one line

rom48.name: CL_SCROLL
rom48.what: scroll B lines of the display up

rom48.name: CL_LINE
rom48.what: clear the bottom B lines

rom48.name: CL_ADDR
rom48.what: B = line counted from the bottom: HL = display address of its start

rom48.name: WAIT_KEY
rom48.what: wait for a key from the current channel

rom48.name: CHAN_OPEN
rom48.what: open channel A (2 = upper screen, 1 = lower screen) before RST 10

rom48.name: BREAK_KEY
rom48.what: carry reset = BREAK (CAPS SHIFT + SPACE) pressed

rom48.name: PR_STRING
rom48.what: print BC characters from DE

rom48.name: PIXEL_ADD
rom48.what: B = y (0 = bottom... 175 - y), C = x: HL = display address, A = x & 7

rom48.name: PIXEL_ADD + 6
rom48.what: entry used by games to skip the y range check: B = y from the top via A

rom48.name: PLOT
rom48.what: BASIC PLOT

rom48.name: PLOT_SUB
rom48.what: plot pixel B = y, C = x with the current OVER / INVERSE

rom48.name: DRAW_ARC
rom48.what: BASIC DRAW x,y,a

rom48.name: DRAW_LINE
rom48.what: draw a line: B = |dy|, C = |dx|, D / E = signs

rom48.name: STACK_A
rom48.what: push A on the calculator stack

rom48.name: STACK_BC
rom48.what: push BC on the calculator stack

rom48.name: PRINT_FP
rom48.what: print the number on the calculator stack

rom48.name: unused block
rom48.what: 0x386E-0x3CFF is all 0xFF in the 48K ROM: where the alt-ROM hooks live. A game may test it as a 48K ROM check (Smash TV)

rom48.name: character set
rom48.what: 96 characters x 8 bytes, space to (c), 0x3D00-0x3FFF; games read it as their font, so an alt ROM must keep it (BRIEFING A3)
